newsitem.title: USA: JLG Industries sees order rate improving.
newsitem.headline: JLG Industries sees order rate improving.

text.p: JLG Industries Inc said Thursday that its order rate should improve, based on customer confidence that domestic rental demand will continue to recover.
The confidence is due in part to the onset of better spring weather and predictions that nonresidential construction activity will remain robust, JLG said.

Although it said its outlook is "somewhat uncertain due to recent order softness," JLG issued a statement saying it believes the fourth quarter will set another record and margins should continue to reflect the same factors as in the third quarter.
Earlier Thursday, JLG reported results for its fiscal third quarter and nine months ended April 30.
Sales for the period were $143.6 million, the highest for any quarter in the company's history and an increase of 27 percent over 1996's third-quarter sales of $113.2 million, the company said.

The company predicted a strong fiscal 1998 as a result of what it called its continued focus on improving production efficiencies, reducing costs and lead-times, growing the business internationally, increasing demand in the marketplace to improve workplace productivity and safety, and introducing new products.
